```{r libraries}
library(tidyverse)
library(clusterProfiler)
library(org.Sc.sgd.db)
library(patchwork)

# org.Sc.sgd.db loads AnnotationDbi, which masks dplyr::select()
select <- dplyr::select

# Shared colour palette for dissertation figures
load(file.path(project_dir, "project_colours.rda"))
```

```{r load-data}
# PCA_genes_AC.txt: gene-level PC scores. PC4 onward is noise-level
# variance, so only PC1/PC2 are carried forward.
pca_genes <- read_tsv(file.path(tables_dir, "PCA_genes_AC.txt"),
                      show_col_types = FALSE)

pca_genes_long <- pca_genes %>%
  select(gene_id, PC1, PC2) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(PC1, PC2), names_to = "PC", values_to = "score")
```

```{r filter-top-bottom-10pct}
# Top/bottom 10% of PC1 and PC2 separately. Hard cutoff limitation
# addressed by GSEA in script 03.
get_top_bottom_10pct <- function(df, pc_name) {
  df_pc <- df %>% filter(PC == pc_name)
  n <- nrow(df_pc)
  cutoff_n <- ceiling(n * 0.1)

  top    <- df_pc %>% slice_max(score, n = cutoff_n) %>% pull(gene_id)
  bottom <- df_pc %>% slice_min(score, n = cutoff_n) %>% pull(gene_id)

  list(top = top, bottom = bottom)
}

pc1_genes <- get_top_bottom_10pct(pca_genes_long, "PC1")
pc2_genes <- get_top_bottom_10pct(pca_genes_long, "PC2")

cat("PC1 top 10%:", length(pc1_genes$top),
    "genes | bottom 10%:", length(pc1_genes$bottom), "genes\n")
cat("PC2 top 10%:", length(pc2_genes$top),
    "genes | bottom 10%:", length(pc2_genes$bottom), "genes\n")
```

```{r run-enrichment-function}
# enrichGO wrapper - background restricted to PCA gene universe to
# avoid inflated significance from unobserved genes
run_go_enrichment <- function(gene_list, universe, label) {
  ego <- enrichGO(
    gene          = gene_list,
    universe      = universe,
    OrgDb         = org.Sc.sgd.db,
    keyType       = "ORF",
    ont           = "ALL",
    pAdjustMethod = "BH",
    pvalueCutoff  = 0.05,
    qvalueCutoff  = 0.2
  )
  cat(label, "-", nrow(as.data.frame(ego)), "enriched terms\n")
  ego
}

all_genes_universe <- pca_genes$gene_id
```

```{r run-pc1}
ego_pc1_top    <- run_go_enrichment(pc1_genes$top,    all_genes_universe, "PC1 top 10%")
ego_pc1_bottom <- run_go_enrichment(pc1_genes$bottom, all_genes_universe, "PC1 bottom 10%")
```

```{r run-pc2}
ego_pc2_top    <- run_go_enrichment(pc2_genes$top,    all_genes_universe, "PC2 top 10%")
ego_pc2_bottom <- run_go_enrichment(pc2_genes$bottom, all_genes_universe, "PC2 bottom 10%")
```

```{r plot-function}
# Single-panel dot plot: top 20 terms by adjusted p-value.
# panel_label: "A" or "B" for patchwork assembly.
# direction_label: short biological description for y-axis title.
#
# CORRECTED: label sizes increased throughout (axis text, axis titles,
# panel tag, legend) per request - previous sizes were tuned for a
# side-by-side layout and looked small once printed/viewed at normal
# scale.
plot_single_panel <- function(ego, panel_label, direction_label, size_limits) {
  df <- as.data.frame(ego)
  if (nrow(df) == 0) return(NULL)

  df_top20 <- df %>%
    arrange(p.adjust) %>%
    slice_head(n = 20) %>%
    mutate(
      Description_short = truncate_wrap_description(Description),
      Description_short = fct_reorder(Description_short, -log10(p.adjust)),
      neg_log10_padj    = -log10(p.adjust)
    )

  ggplot(df_top20, aes(x = neg_log10_padj, y = Description_short,
                       size = Count)) +
    geom_point(color = project_colours[["pink"]]) +
    # CORRECTED: explicit shared limits/breaks so panel A and panel B
    # use the identical size scale - previously each panel picked its
    # own Count range automatically, and since the two ranges differ,
    # patchwork's guides = "collect" couldn't merge them into one
    # legend and instead showed two separate ones, with the second
    # running off the edge of the combined image.
    scale_size_continuous(limits = size_limits, range = c(1, 8)) +
    labs(
      tag  = panel_label,
      x    = expression(-log[10]("adjusted p-value")),
      y    = direction_label,
      size = "Gene count"
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 22) +
    theme(
      axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 19, colour = "black"),
      axis.text.x  = element_text(size = 18, colour = "black"),
      axis.title   = element_text(size = 22, colour = "black"),
      axis.title.y = element_text(size = 19, face = "italic",
                                  color = "grey40"),
      plot.tag     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 26),
      legend.text  = element_text(size = 17),
      legend.title = element_text(size = 19)
    )
}

# Combine top and bottom panels (A above, B below) into one figure via
# patchwork, with a shared legend. Stacked vertically (rather than
# side-by-side) so the combined figure fills roughly one page when
# printed, per request. Returns a plot object ready for ggsave.
#
# CORRECTED: computes shared size_limits across BOTH panels' Count
# values before plotting either one, so scale_size_continuous() above
# gets the same range in both calls and guides = "collect" can
# actually merge them into a single legend instead of duplicating it.
make_combined_figure <- function(ego_top, ego_bottom,
                                 label_top, label_bottom
                                 ) {
  df_top    <- as.data.frame(ego_top)
  df_bottom <- as.data.frame(ego_bottom)
  all_counts <- c(df_top$Count, df_bottom$Count)
  shared_size_limits <- range(all_counts, na.rm = TRUE)

  p_top    <- plot_single_panel(ego_top,    "A", label_top,    shared_size_limits)
  p_bottom <- plot_single_panel(ego_bottom, "B", label_bottom, shared_size_limits)

 combined <- ((p_top / p_bottom) +
               plot_layout(guides = "collect")) &
            theme(legend.position = "bottom")

  combined
}
```

```{r figure-9-pc1, fig.width=10, fig.height=24}
# Figure 9: PC1, TOR/PKA signalling axis.
# Panel A (top): top 10%, active TOR/PKA signalling.
# Panel B (bottom): bottom 10%, TOR/PKA inhibited.
fig9 <- make_combined_figure(
  ego_top    = ego_pc1_top,
  ego_bottom = ego_pc1_bottom,
  label_top    = paste0(
    "Top 10% PC1 (n = ", length(pc1_genes$top), " genes) — ",
    "active TOR/PKA signalling state"
  ),
  label_bottom = paste0(
    "Bottom 10% PC1 (n = ", length(pc1_genes$bottom), " genes) — ",
    "TOR/PKA-inhibited state"
  )
)

print(fig9)

```

```{r figure-10-pc2, fig.width=10, fig.height=24}
# Figure 10: PC2, cell-size axis (large vs small cells)
# Panel A (top): top 10%, large cells.
# Panel B (bottom): bottom 10%, small cells.
fig10 <- make_combined_figure(
  ego_top    = ego_pc2_top,
  ego_bottom = ego_pc2_bottom,
  label_top    = paste0(
    "Top 10% PC2 (n = ", length(pc2_genes$top), " genes) — ",
    "upregulated in large cells"
  ),
  label_bottom = paste0(
    "Bottom 10% PC2 (n = ", length(pc2_genes$bottom), " genes) — ",
    "upregulated in small cells"
  )
)

print(fig10)

```

```{r save-outputs}
# Save results tables
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc1_top),
          file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc1_top10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc1_bottom),
          file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc1_bottom10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc2_top),
          file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc2_top10pct.txt"))
write_tsv(as.data.frame(ego_pc2_bottom),
          file.path(output_dir, "go_clusterprofiler_pc2_bottom10pct.txt"))

# Save combined figures - now tall/stacked (A above B) rather than
# wide/side-by-side, so width/height swapped to suit a portrait,
# roughly one-page layout when printed.
if (!is.null(fig9)) {
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "figure9_go_clusterprofiler_pc1.png"),
         plot = fig9, width = 10, height = 24, dpi = 300)
}

if (!is.null(fig10)) {
  ggsave(file.path(figures_dir, "figure10_go_clusterprofiler_pc2.png"),
         plot = fig10, width = 10, height = 24, dpi = 300)
}

cat("Done - results saved to output_tables/ and figures/\n")
```
